description: OpenDSM, formerly OpenEEmeter, is a Python library maintained by the OpenDSM community to estimate the effects of demand-side energy programmes. Statistical models fit historical metered consumption and predict counterfactual usage for comparison with observed post-intervention consumption. The repository documents daily, monthly billing and hourly models, including solar-aware energy-efficiency and demand-response variants. It also provides data-sufficiency checks, model serialisation and warnings. Geographic coverage depends on the supplied meter and temperature series; the README describes broader weather coverage as future work, so a global weather service is not implied. Public source and package-installation instructions are available free under Apache-2.0. A material caveat is that changing default settings or bypassing sufficiency checks produces results outside OpenDSM-compliant measurement. An experimental solar-installation feature and an unfinished demand-response update are explicitly distinguished from established methods. The models support building-retrofit evaluation and demand estimates for grid studies. They complement physical building simulation in EnergyPlus (model-energyplus), not reproducing its component-level heat balances.
